thread_analysis.thread_summary: Alinco Incorporated (contact Mitsunori Kirimoto) works with Allion (Itsuo Sakai, Masaya Iida) across two engagements years apart: a detailed 2020 registration troubleshooting saga for module XE1134 (Bluetooth Core Spec 4.2) involving TCRL/Layer Selection setup guidance and recovery from a premature submission with unresolved ICS errors, and a 2025 follow-up inquiry about registering a similar but updated module (same function as XE1134, IC changed from CSR8670 to QCC3044) where the customer, having forgotten much of the process after years away, requested a refresher consultation.
all_questions_found: What should I do with the TCRL warning, Update TCRL option, and Layer Selection items during project setup? (see thread_0262_case_01)
How do I recover from a locked, under-review project after submitting with unresolved ICS errors? (see thread_0262_case_02)
(2025, administrative) Can we have a refresher Teams/F2F consultation before proceeding with a new, similar registration after years away?
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: This thread preserves detailed, hands-on registration-execution guidance (TCRL handling, Layer Selection pruning, ICS Consistency Check error types, and the critical BQA Project Return recovery procedure) that remains directly applicable to the customer's 2025 follow-up project, since the underlying registration site mechanics described are foundational rather than specific to the original 2020 module.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: The original 2020 customer submission proceeded with visible ICS errors despite the registration site's own checkbox warning, leading to the costly locked-state situation — a reminder that customers should be explicitly warned not to proceed past a visible Consistency Check error regardless of time pressure, since recovery requires an extra BQA request cycle.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: For customers returning to do a new but similar registration years after a previous engagement, proactively offer a refresher consultation (Teams or in-person) before diving into registration-site mechanics, since customers can easily forget critical, non-obvious steps (TCRL handling, Layer Selection pruning) that aren't intuitive from the registration site's own interface and warning messages.
